rv.q: Where “King Liz” disappoints is in its sometimes ham-handed plotting.
But the dramaturgy is woefully shaky, with over-the-top characterizations and unforgivable lapses of basic logic.
As sports-related plays go, this is one of the better ones we've seen in recent seasons.
Even if "King Liz" seems overstuffed or schematic, every time Karen Pittman takes the court, the crowd goes wild.
The greatest glory in “King Liz” is reserved for the title character, and Karen Pittman does her full justice.
But Coppel only partially delivers on her promise to bring a new lens to the play's timely topics of race and gender.
The overstuffed and tonally jumbled play by Fernanda Coppel needs that assist as familiar themes dribble out.
Though it may not quite be a slam dunk, King Liz takes a difficult shot and ultimately scores.
If Fernanda Coppel’s writing is somewhat overblown, director Lisa Peterson does nothing to rein it in.
I really thought King Liz was bold, smart and told me a story I haven't seen depicted on stage before.
